threads.body: In `testCaptureGcCauseCanBeDisabled`, `java17Config` is returned from `getInstrumentationConfig(...)` but never stubbed. If `Internal.configure(...)` reads `enabled`/`capture_gc_cause` from `java17Config` on some runtimes, Mockito will return default values (often `false`) and the callback may never be invoked, making the test fail. Consider stubbing `java17Config.getBoolean(...)` as well, or returning the same fully-stubbed `config` for both `runtime_telemetry` and `runtime_telemetry_java17`.

In `testCaptureGcCauseCanBeDisabled`, `java17Config` is returned from `getInstrumentationConfig(...)` but never stubbed. If `Internal.configure(...)` reads `enabled`/`capture_gc_cause` from `java17Config` on some runtimes, Mockito will return default values (often `false`) and the callback may never be invoked, making the test fail. Consider stubbing `java17Config.getBoolean(...)` as well, or returning the same fully-stubbed `config` for both `runtime_telemetry` and `runtime_telemetry_java17`.

`testCaptureGcCauseDefaultsToTrue` calls `Internal.configure(...)` without controlling `DeclarativeConfigUtil`/config inputs. If this code consults system/env properties, the test can become environment-dependent (e.g., if `capture_gc_cause` is set to false externally) and fail unexpectedly. Consider mocking `DeclarativeConfigUtil.getInstrumentationConfig(...)` to return a controlled `DeclarativeConfigProperties` that does not override `capture_gc_cause`, or explicitly clearing/restoring the relevant property sources within the test.

The warning text is a bit ambiguous: what's deprecated is the ability to set the property to `false`, not 'disabling' in general. To make the operational message clearer, consider wording it like: \"Setting otel.instrumentation.runtime-telemetry.capture-gc-cause=false is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0; GC cause will always be captured.\"

threads.body: `capture_gc_cause` deprecation detection is currently based on `config.getString("capture_gc_cause")`, which will likely be `null` for a boolean property, so the warning may never be emitted. Also, `SemconvStability.v3Preview() || ...` makes an explicit opt-out (`capture_gc_cause=false`) ineffective when v3 preview is enabled, which conflicts with the PR description’s “explicit opt-out” requirement. Consider reading the nullable Boolean once, warning when it’s present, and using it to override the default.

replies.body:
Fixed the warning detection: it now reads the nullable `config.getBoolean("capture_gc_cause")` once and warns when the property is present (the previous `getString` check returned null for a boolean property, so the warning never fired).

The opt-out being ineffective under v3preview is intentional — GC cause is now unconditional once stable JVM semantic conventions are emitted (it's no longer configurable then). The `capture_gc_cause` option only applies before v3preview/3.0. I've updated the PR description to match.
